intro: Three people on one lease, and the lowest per-person cost you can get near WashU (Washington University in St. Louis) without sharing a bedroom. The 3 bedroom is how most junior-year groups do it.

Below is every live 3 bedroom with its walk time to campus and reviews from students who lived there. One warning worth taking seriously: group leases live and die on the landlord. Read the reviews before you fall in love with the porch.
directAnswer: 3 bedroom apartments near WashU are mostly houses and flats in Skinker-DeBaliviere and University City, MO, plus the blocks near the Delmar Loop. Every rent on this page is live, and splitting three ways is how groups get the lowest per-person cost near campus.

faqs.q: How much is a 3 bedroom near WashU per person?
faqs.a: Divide the whole-unit rent by three and add utilities if they’re separate. Better-located or more updated 3 bedrooms near WashU cost more, so use the listings above to compare actual prices.

faqs.q: When do groups need to have a lease signed?
faqs.a: Earlier than you think. Students report private landlords start signing around November for next August, and the well located 3 bedrooms are the first inventory to disappear, because every group of three wants the same ten blocks. Get your group and budget agreed by October and you'll have real options.

faqs.q: Joint lease or individual leases: which is better for a group?
faqs.a: A joint lease makes the whole group responsible together, which is simpler but means a flaky housemate becomes everyone's problem. Individual leases separate your liability but are rarer here outside the big student buildings. Check which structure each listing uses, and run it through Lease Check before anyone signs.

faqs.q: What should a group check before signing?
faqs.a: The landlord's reputation above everything: reviews on the listing, how fast maintenance happens, whether previous tenants got their deposit back. Then the boring things that bite groups, like the subleasing rules for summer, who handles lawn or snow on a house, exactly which utilities land on you.

benchmarkNote: Rents on this page are each listing's current asking rent. Proximity does not publish averages computed from its own listings.
